reconstructionScope: Type 88-II scout. The museum model serial 12 and appearance are a reference choice, not a verified Uchida squadron aircraft. No light-bomber extra centre struts or bomb racks.

historicalReferences.scope: Museum 1/20 Type 88-II model, Motokoka 2020-06-09, CC BY-SA 4.0; appearance only
Historical Type II photographs; mixed variants screened. kda2-11 supports the front/side form and kda2-20 shows the doubled V tailplane braces.
Explicit Type II secondary specification: span15m, length12.28m, nominal height3.38m; factory dimension drawing not acquired
Original PDF page5/printed51 visually read; research cites 10thDivision Type88x12 but notes AirCorps Type94 record conflict. Does not identify our subtype/serial/colour

inferences: Airfoil section, slight dihedral and unseen structural sections remain image-derived.
Hidden cockpit equipment and hardware arrangement are reconstruction choices.
Uncalibrated museum photograph informs colour relationships; it does not prove wartime paint reflectance.
Propeller diameter follows the main image proportions; a secondary 3.3m statement has not been checked against a factory drawing.
Alternative generic length12.80m, kit span15.2m and a 1933 Flight transcription disagree; chosen anchors are the table explicitly labelled II, without averaging.
Illegible tiny service marks are represented as linework, not claimed transcriptions.
Lower-wing underside roundel placement is inferred; these surfaces are not visible in the primary museum photograph.
Fixed tailplane yaw -2.0733553deg and height2.135m are a photographic installation fit, not an original-aircraft specification.
Reference rudder pose13.55deg is explicitly shown by the real comparison control; the source and exports remain neutral.
Upper rudder and outer elevator forward balances are cross-checked with TypeII photographs; TypeI drawings only corroborate the mechanism, not TypeII dimensions.

paintContours.scope: Four legible wing numeral contours and seven visible tail-ink components; opposite tail side inferred. Constant authored paint, no source photographic illumination.
